sd_hornets_nest.blurb: Hornets Nest is a big granite formation in the South Seas section of the Needles, near Mount Rushmore in the Black Hills. It stands on the left as you enter the South Seas clearing, facing Shipyard Rock. Sixteen routes split into eleven sport lines and five trad, running from the 5.6 range up to 5.13, with the bulk of them at 5.11 and 5.12 and only a handful of easier warm-ups. Most lines need little more than a rack of quickdraws, though a few want extra gear. A path circles the base to reach routes that do not start from the front. Get down by rappelling from fixed anchors, and bring two ropes.

sd_border_wall_bouldering.blurb: The Border Wall is a roadside bouldering spot on the hill leading up toward Mount Rushmore, in the Black Hills. It holds sixteen problems, from an easy V1 up to a couple of V10s, with a cluster of moderate V2 to V4 lines and a stiff band of V6 to V8 problems in between. The main face is steep, around 45 degrees, with small holds, and it rewards strong fingers; topping out can feel committed. It faces south, so summer afternoons turn it hot, while it dries out fast after winter weather. Reaching it takes a short uphill walk from a pullout beside the highway.

sd_north_wall_the.blurb: The North Wall is a limestone sport crag in the VC zone outside Rapid City, reached by a walk past the Main and Sniper Walls and then a switchbacking climb up the hillside. All sixteen routes are bolted, with one at 5.9, four at 5.10, five at 5.11 and six at 5.12, so it suits climbers working through the middle grades and beyond. The stone is solid and the wall sits in shade through most of the day, with a little early sun possible near midsummer. That makes it a pleasant choice when other walls are baking.

sd_hall_of_truth_corridor.blurb: Hall of Truth Corridor is a narrow descending gully at Breezy Point in the Needles near Mount Rushmore, lined with granite routes. Sixteen climbs, fourteen of them sport and two trad, run from 5.7 to about 5.11, with the largest group around 5.9. The gully divides into a wider, sunnier upper hall and a tighter, shadier lower hall, and a more open outer section sits behind the lower hall. Getting between the sections involves a few fourth-class chimney moves. Routes are fairly short, so it works well for a quick session of moderate sport climbing in a quiet spot.

sd_community_cove.blurb: Community Cove is a corner of the Dells of the Sioux River recreation area near Dell Rapids in eastern South Dakota, where a gorge cuts through Sioux quartzite. It mixes eight sport routes, several of which also work as top-ropes, with eight boulder problems. Sport lines run from easy 5.x up to low 5.11, mostly in the 5.5 to 5.9 range, while the problems stay mainly V2 with a few harder outliers. The quartzite gives faces, cracks and crimps. A homemade wooden ladder near the parking area drops down to extra boulders along the riverbank. It is a handy spot for a mixed day with a group of differing abilities.

sd_big_black_face.blurb: Big Black Face is the main wall of the Sunshine area in Spearfish Canyon, in the northern Black Hills. Fifteen sport routes climb pocketed limestone, with most sitting in the 5.10 band and a smaller group at 5.9 and 5.11, plus one easier line and one 5.12. The obvious face carries thirteen or fourteen bolted lines, so it is compact and efficient. It is described as a good warm-up for strong climbers and an enjoyable day for newer ones. It is only a few minutes along the base, heading left, once the Sunshine trail reaches the cliff. Winter days can still be pleasant here, though snow on the ground is possible.

sd_hobgoblin_s_hideout.blurb: Hobgoblin's Hideout is a small cliff at Palisades State Park near Garretson, where Split Rock Creek has carved a gorge in Sioux quartzite. It holds fifteen climbs, ten trad and five top-rope, mostly easy to moderate: a spread from low fifth class up to 5.9, with the bulk between 5.7 and 5.9. It receives little sun and can stay damp after heavy rain, so fall and spring are the comfortable seasons. Its position between neighbouring formations makes it a calmer option when the main part of the park fills with visitors. Approach by following the trail upstream from South Wall, staying close to the cliff.

sd_abominable_snowman.blurb: Abominable Snowman is a blade of granite on the northern side of the Monster area in the Needles, close to Mount Rushmore. Fifteen routes, thirteen sport and two trad, range from 5.8 to about 5.12, with a good concentration at 5.10 to 5.12. The routes are fairly long and the wall sees little traffic, with newer bolted lines sitting beside older climbs. The walk in from the Monster sign-in board is a scrappy one: it involves a bouldery gully, some easy scrambling and a corridor, ending at a gravelly, worn base. It rewards climbers who want a quieter day on solid sport lines.
